articles.title: US midterms 2026: Polling guru Allan Lichtman, who accurately predicted 9 of last 11 presidential races, sees headwinds for Democrats
articles.summary: Allan Lichtman, the renowned political historian and forecaster, analyzes the upcoming 2026 midterm elections, predicting a Democratic surge against the Republicans, driven by low approval ratings for Trump.
articles.body: Historian Allan Lichtman, who predicted nine of the last 11 US presidential elections correctly, expects Democrats to take control of both chambers of Congress in next week's midterm elections, forecasting a setback for President Donald Trump's Republican Party.Lichtman, a professor at American University in Washington, DC, said national polling, Trump's approval ratings, voter enthusiasm and early voting trends indicate that Democrats are gaining ground ahead of the November 3 elections.In an interview with The Times (UK), Lichtman said the political environment was particularly unfavourable for Republicans, pointing to the president's low approval ratings and the historical losses suffered by the party controlling the White House during midterm elections."When the approval rating for a president is as low as Trump's, on average the White House party loses 40 House and six Senate seats," Lichtman said. He clarified that the figures were not his prediction but an indication of the political conditions facing Republicans.Lichtman said Democrats currently hold an advantage of seven to 11% points over Republicans in the generic congressional ballot, which measures voter preferences for which party should control Congress. He considers this measure a more reliable indicator than polls focused on individual races.He also pointed to a shift in voter enthusiasm. While Republicans typically record higher turnout, Lichtman said Democrats appeared more motivated this time. He added that early voting figures were also favourable to the party.The historian puts Democrats' chances of winning control of the Senate at 67%, with a 51-49 majority his most likely outcome.Republicans currently hold a 53-47 advantage in the Senate, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. Lichtman expects the party to make gains in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas while retaining its seat in Michigan. He also identified Alaska as a potential Democratic pickup, with former Representative Mary Peltola among the candidates he expects to benefit.He pointed to the competitiveness of races in traditionally Republican states as another indication of the changing political landscape."It's amazing that Democrats are competitive in South Carolina, which Trump won by 18 points," he said. "Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since the Great Depression in 1932 and yet that's a neck-and-neck race, as is Iowa."Lichtman also expects Democrats to take control of the House, where Republicans currently hold a narrow 218-214 majority. He puts the party's chances of winning the chamber at more than 90%.He attributed some of the Republican Party's difficulties to what he described as weak candidates, naming Ken Paxton in Texas, Roger Marshall in Kansas and Darline Graham in South Carolina.The historian also criticised the influence of wealthy donours and outside spending in the election campaigns. He argued that large financial contributions were affecting the political contest and pointed to billionaire Elon Musk's support for Republican candidates.Lichtman compared the current political climate to the 1966 midterm elections, when Democrats suffered major losses under then-President Lyndon B Johnson amid growing opposition to the Vietnam War and domestic unrest.His latest assessment comes after he incorrectly predicted that Democratic candidate Kamala Harris would defeat Trump in the 2024 presidential election. He also missed the outcome of the 2000 race between Al Gore and George W Bush.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Turbulence continues for Saudi flyers as Air India extends flight curbs till Nov 14
articles.summary: Air India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia until November 14 amid growing unrest in West Asia.
articles.body: Air India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia until November 14 amid growing unrest in West Asia. The extension covers services connecting Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam.Earlier, IndiGo cancelled flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until November 14. Akasa Air also announced suspension of flights connecting Riyadh until November 30 and Jeddah until November 10.Air India announced the decision on Friday, citing the prevailing situation in the region. The two airlines had earlier cancelled services to Riyadh and Dammam until November 7, while flights to Jeddah were suspended until October 31."Due to the prevailing situation in the region, Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 14 November 2026 (inclusive)," Air India said in a post on X.Passengers with confirmed bookings issued on or before October 30 for travel up to November 14 can avail themselves of a one-time complimentary rebooking, subject to availability. They can reschedule their journeys for travel up to November 29 or opt for a full refund upon cancellation."Air India guests may rebook to or from any operational Air India station in Saudi Arabia, while Air India Express guests may rebook to or from any operational Air India Express station in Saudi Arabia or Bahrain," the airline said.The flight suspensions come amid heightened security concerns in West Asia, with Saudi Arabia reporting fresh Houthi activity. On Friday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels near Mecca, Islam's holiest city.Coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. articles.title: BAU adopts Bhagalpur village to promote Jardalu mango
articles.summary: BAU Bhagalpur adopts Pansalla village to promote GI-tagged Jardalu mango, planting 100 saplings and aiming to develop a “Jardalu Mango Gaon” hub.
articles.body: Bhagalpur: Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Bhagalpur, has adopted Pansalla village in Katahara panchayat of Sultanganj block under its Village Adoption Programme (VAP) to promote the cultivation of the GI-tagged Jardalu mango. The university plans to develop the village as a dedicated Jardalu mango-growing hub, which it hopes will eventually be known as ‘Jardalu Mango Gaon’.The initiative aims to promote the distinctive mango variety of Bhagalpur, disseminate scientific horticultural practices among farmers, increase their income through mango cultivation and create new livelihood opportunities.BAU vice-chancellor D R Singh said the university had adopted nearly 108 hectares of Pansalla village, which has around 350 households and a population of about 1,500, to promote Jardalu cultivation.“The objective is to develop the village as a model for Jardalu mango cultivation, considering the favourable climatic conditions, nutrient-rich soil and willingness of local farmers to take up horticulture,” Singh said.As an initial step, BAU distributed and planted 100 Jardalu mango saplings on farmers’ agricultural land and encouraged them to take up orchard-based cultivation. Further activities under the programme would be taken up in phases, Singh said.The initiative also seeks to improve cultivation practices, promote orchard-based livelihoods and strengthen the regional identity and market reach of the GI-tagged mango variety.Tracing the variety’s history, Singh said Jardalu had been cultivated in the Bhagalpur region for more than 200 years. The tradition is associated with old mother trees and cultivation practices in villages around Sultanganj, Mahesi and the adjoining Gangetic alluvial belt.Ashok Chaudhary, popularly known as the ‘Mango Man of Bihar’, said preserving the distinct identity and quality of Jardalu mango was as important as promoting its scientific cultivation. “Farmers need access to improved production techniques. Expanding Jardalu cultivation can help raise their incomes and strengthen the agricultural identity of the region,” he said.Pansalla mukhiya Chandan Kumar and village resident and former BAU dean (agriculture) Mukteshwar Kumar welcomed the initiative, saying it would encourage farmers to set up new mango orchards and strengthen the village’s association with the Jardalu variety.Anita Kumari, senior scientist and head of the Krishi Vigyan Kendra, said the collaboration between BAU and the rural community would improve farmers’ access to scientific agricultural and horticultural practices. articles.title: CM Vijay announces 5-year age relaxation for govt jobs in Tamil Nadu; check revised age limits
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday ordered a five-year relaxation in the upper age limit for government jobs, offering relief to
articles.body: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday ordered a five-year relaxation in the upper age limit for government jobs, offering relief to aspirants appearing for competitive examinations. The relaxation will remain in force for five years, the state government said.The decision was taken in response to representations from government job aspirants seeking additional time to compete for government positions, according to an official release, news agency PTI reported."The age relaxation will be over and above the extant norms that govern age relaxations," the release added.Under the revised norms, the upper age limit for Group-I services will increase from 32 to 37 years for General Category candidates and from 37 to 42 years for reserved category candidates.For differently-abled candidates applying under Group-I services, the upper age limit for the General category will increase from 42 to 47 years, while that for reserved category candidates will go up from 47 to 52 years, the release said.For Group-II and Group-II-A services, reserved category candidates will continue to have no upper age limit. However, the limit for General category candidates will increase from 30 to 35 years.Similarly, for differently abled candidates belonging to the General category, the upper age limit for these posts will be raised from 40 to 45 years, PTI reported.The government release cited these categories as examples of how the five-year relaxation would be applied over and above the existing age limits prescribed for different services and social categories.The revised relaxation will be applicable for five years and will be in addition to the age concessions already available under existing rules, the government said.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Dolly Parton started giving free books to children 31 years ago; a new October 29 report says her Knox County programme attracted nearly 950 sign-ups in August and raised over $150,000 following her death
articles.summary: More than 30 years after country music legend Dolly Parton started her childhood reading programme, a wave of public support following her death in August
articles.body: More than 30 years after country music legend Dolly Parton started her childhood reading programme, a wave of public support following her death in August has led to record numbers of new registrations and large donations to the charity's local branch in her home state of Tennessee. A report published on 29 October 2026 by East Tennessee television station WVLT reveals that the Imagination Library chapter in Knox County registered nearly 950 new children in August alone. The record increase in registrations came alongside a fundraising campaign that brought in more than $150,000 (around £115,000) for the local branch. The rise in donations followed a public request from Parton's family. They asked fans to honour her memory by supporting the charity instead of sending flowers.Local fundraising cuts annual targets in halfThe Imagination Library of Knox County depends on donations from the local community to pay for its work. The State of Tennessee matches local donations dollar-for-dollar. The Knox County chapter needs to raise around $288,000 each year to receive the state funding. This brings its total yearly operating budget to nearly $600,000. According to figures reported by WVLT, the fundraising campaign following Parton's death on 25 August raised more than $150,000 in just a few weeks. This covered about half of the local chapter's yearly fundraising target in a single month. The donations included $25,000 given directly between 25 August and 22 September. This amount was enough to provide monthly books to more than 1,500 children for a full year. The annual Seeds of Imagination fundraising luncheon also raised more than $109,000. The money will support nearly 7,000 children. In addition, the first "Give Like Dolly Day" raised another $12,000. Organisers now plan to make the event an annual tradition.Inspired by family and delivered to mailboxesParton first started the Imagination Library 31 years ago, in 1995, to help children in her hometown area of Sevier County, Tennessee. The idea came from her father, Robert Lee Parton. She often described him as one of the smartest people she had ever known, even though he could not read or write. Under the programme, every registered child receives one free book each month. The books are chosen according to the child's age and delivered directly to their home mailbox. The service begins at birth and continues until the child turns five. Every child starts the programme with a welcome copy of the classic children's story The Little Engine That Could. According to Kay Hurst, programme manager for the Imagination Library of Knox County, every book sent through the programme across North America receives its final mailing label at Direct Mail Services facilities in Knox County before entering the postal system. To keep costs low, Parton made bulk production agreements with publishing companies. These deals brought the average cost of providing and mailing each book down to around $2.60.A global operation with growing demandWhat began as a small programme in rural East Tennessee has grown into a worldwide effort. The Imagination Library now operates in five countries, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and the Republic of Ireland. So far, the charity has sent more than 300 million books to children around the world. It currently mails out more than three million books every month. In Knox County alone, the local programme has distributed more than 4.1 million books to preschool children since it began. Publishing company Penguin Random House has been the charity's only publishing partner for 27 years. According to its comments in the WVLT report, the company is seeing growing demand for the programme across the country. It has ordered additional print runs to make sure there are enough books for the rising number of registered families. A special committee from the Dollywood Foundation works with reading experts, teachers and child development specialists to choose the books. Lisa Vitelli, Vice President and Director of Premium Literacy Sales at Penguin Random House, said committee members read every book aloud before deciding whether to include it in the programme. This helps them choose stories that interest young children and encourage them to read the books again and again.Visual artist Dan Santat, who created new illustrations for The Little Engine That Could for modern readers, said updating classic children's books helps them connect with younger generations. With the total number of books distributed in Knox County now exceeding four million, local organisers say Parton's original goal of helping children develop a love of reading continues to reach thousands of families.You use AI every day.
